title: Breeding-aware Revenue Maximization for NFT Viral Marketing on Social Networks

problem.claim: Maximize NFT marketplace revenue by selecting users for NFT airdrop campaigns and determining the quantities of NFTs to release.

gap.claim: NFT scarcity, rarity, and breeding mechanisms create challenges for viral marketing strategies.

contributions.claim: Introduces the NFT Revenue Maximization problem for NFT marketplaces.
Proves the hardness of NFT Revenue Maximization and proposes the Quantity and Offspring-Oriented Airdrops approximation algorithm.
Uses scarcity-conscious revenue, valuation-based quantity inequality, and incentives for Rare Trait Collectors to improve airdrop selection, quantity pruning, and breeding-related revenue.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments show that QOOA produces up to 3.8 times the revenue of baseline methods in large-scale social networks.

narrative_sequence.summary: NFT promotion and revenue generation rely heavily on social networks.
NFT scarcity, rarity, and breeding mechanisms complicate viral marketing.
The paper formulates NFT Revenue Maximization around user selection and NFT release quantities.
It establishes hardness and proposes QOOA with scarcity-, valuation-, and breeding-aware mechanisms.
The authors report higher revenue than baselines in large-scale social networks.

source_observation.claim: The method prunes suboptimal airdrops and quantities early using scarcity-conscious revenue and valuation-based quantity inequality.

interpretation.claim: Domain-specific value and scarcity constraints can guide early search reduction in viral marketing optimization.

application.claim: Use value-aware pruning rules before evaluating candidate campaigns when optimizing scarce digital goods.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether these pruning rules generalize beyond NFT marketing.

source_observation.claim: QOOA incentivizes collectors to acquire multiple NFTs with rare traits to facilitate high-value offspring through breeding.

interpretation.claim: Marketing optimization can account for downstream value created by user actions rather than only immediate acquisition revenue.

application.claim: Model delayed or compositional value when campaign actions enable valuable future products or interactions.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the breeding model, incentives, or conditions under which offspring value increases.

unknowns: The approximation guarantee and hardness classification are unspecified.
The baselines, datasets, experimental protocol, and statistical details are unspecified.
The mechanism for computing scarcity-conscious revenue and valuation-based quantity inequality is unspecified.
